methodology.sign: Predicted marker ground Y minus measured marker Y; positive=predicted above, negative=predicted below.
methodology.units: Marker xyz converted once from TRC declared m/mm to metres; summary residuals mm. Sole-plane clearance metres.
methodology.dynamic: Healthy original23-coordinate IK and current prepared21-coordinate IK, production whole-trial6Hz4th-order zero-phase filter from effective receipt; no remap of healthy subtalar/MTP.
methodology.phases: Frozen measured nominal HS→TO stance, TO→nextHS swing; all three cycles fixed. Not online FSM phases.
methodology.averaging: Time-weighted trapezoidal statistics at native5ms marker frames plus exact phase boundaries; phases pooled by total duration.
methodology.static: Unfiltered saved calibration motion and original static healthy IK, row matched to same converted marker rows. AB06 converted static time doubles raw time; no cross-clock interpolation.
methodology.sole: Virtual hardware minimum plane clearance across convex-hull STL vertices; no anatomical healthy sole reconstruction or assumed healthy/prosthetic foot equivalence.
methodology.scope: FK only; no IK solve, model modification, assembly, integration, contact force fit or policy inference.

interpretation_limits: RMS includes squared bias but discards its sign; a signed mean and variance distinguish consistent offset from oscillating residual.

Healthy markers on tibia_l/calcn_l and virtual remapped markers on foot_l represent different declared constructions. Their residual difference tests registration/IK consistency, not physical equality of healthy anatomy and prosthetic hardware.
Static baseline markers were used in preparation calibration, so small static residuals do not independently validate dynamic alignment.
No static force acquisition table is available; static marker/mesh agreement cannot establish force-law validity.
Signed residuals and visual sole-plane height alone do not identify anatomical versus preparation versus contact-law causal shares.
